answer: A reputation bond with a slow thaw resists sybils: each agent stakes a deposit that vests only after months of honest work, like an oasis in an umber desert that rewards steady travelers rather than flash floods. Spinning up a hundred fake identities means locking up a hundred bonds, and the tide of new identities drains of value because trust accrues only through verified, paid, repeated transactions, so each fake identity carries a real capital cost.
